label: English Women on Balconies
name: English Women on Balconies
text: Undefined place, here given: Aldersgate Street, where many inns and taverns were located.
src_text_orig: vntenher vor den Wohnstuben stehen überall schöne eiserne balcons oder lauben herauß daß man auß den Zimmeren auff selbige hinaußgehen vnd sonderlich das schöne Englische frauenzimmer sich auff denselbigen bequemlich schau-stellen kan, haben auch dise commoditet, daß man auf den gassen am schärmen darunter hinpassiren kan; So hangen auch von allen haüsern schöne vnd prächtige tavernes oder schilten herauß, darunter vil von vilem eisenwerk vnd schöner mahlereÿ so groß vnd kostbar, daß ein einiger offt auf 100. pfund Sterling kostet, dises machet nun einem beÿ dem eintritt vnd eingang in solche  gassen einen schönen vnd prächtigen anblik; die innwendige commoditet der haüser besteht meistens darinn daß vil haüser ihre eigene brunnen in den kuchen haben.
src_text_translation: In front of the parlours there are beautiful iron balconies or arbours everywhere, so that one can walk out of the rooms onto them and, in particular, the beautiful English women can conveniently flaunt themselves on them; they also have the convenience that one can pass sheltered underneath them in the streets. All the houses have beautiful and splendid inn signs or signboards hanging out of them, among them many of fine ironwork or beautiful painting so large and precious that a few often cost 100 pound sterling. This makes a beautiful and splendid sight when entering such alleys; the internal convenience of the houses usually consists in the fact that many houses have their own wells in the kitchens.

label: Of English Men and Women
name: Of English Men and Women
text: Undefined place, here given: Lincoln's Inn field, the largest public square in London.
src_text_orig: Die Engelländer insgemein sind vil geistreicher vnd gegen den frembden vil discreter vnd höfflicher als die holländer, vnd ist sonderlich das Englische frauenzimmer gar galant vnd höfflich, leben (auch nachdem sie schon verheürahtet) in aller freÿheit, sitzen in ihren köstlichen läden gleich Princessinnen herrlich aufgebutzet gantz still vnd müssig, fahren öffters spatzieren ja werden von ihren Männern selbsten den fremmden öffters dazu presentieret, daß sie demnach in völliger freÿheit aller selbstbeliebigen wollust nach wunsch pflegen mögen, vnd die Engelländer selbst daher ein sprichwort haben, daß gut wäre, daß kein bruk übers meer seÿ, sonst die weiber alle auß gantz Europa in Engelland übergelauffen kommen wurden.
src_text_translation: The English are in general much more witty and much more dircreet and polite towards foreigners than the Dutch; and, in particular, are the English ladies very gallant and polite, they live (even after getting married) in total freedom, sitting in their wonderful shops much like princesses magificantly dressed up completelly silent and idle, they often leave for a stroll, yes, they are, at times, even presented by their own husbands to strangers. Thus, they enjoy complete liberty to indulge in whatever pleasures they desire, and the English themselves therefore have a saying, that it is good that there is no bridge leading across the sea, for otherwise, women from all of Europe would overrun England.

label: Black People
name: Black People
text:
Undefined place, here given: St Botolph. Black people and communites were spread all over Restoration London and not contained to one area, St. Botolph is one of the oldest known locations of a small Black community.

Warning: Racism
Despite Bucher's, sadly, unsurprisingly racist description of Black people, this is quite a remarkable occurence, as he is, so far, our only Swiss traveller remarking on the diversity of London. Since the 1600s, London has always been an incredibly diverse space. Bucher's account bears witness not only to this diversity, but also that, according to Bucher, many Black Londoners were successful and an integrated and visible part of London's public life.
Further reading on this topic: Newman, Simon P. Freedom Seekers: Escaping from Slavery in Restoration London. University of London Press, 2022.

Fontanges were a popular high headress made of linen and lace.
src_text_orig: Es sind auch sehr vil Mohren Mann = vnd Weibspersonen in Londen, darunter auch etliche reiche Kauffleüt, vnd ist wol lächerlich zu sehen, wie das frauenzimmer mit schönen weissen Fontangen über dem brantschwartzen angesicht prangend daherzeücht.
src_text_translation: There are also many black men and women in London, including quite a few rich merchants, and it is quite ridiculous to see the women flaunt around with beautiful white fontanges above their black faces.
